summary.intent: Reconcile Callisto docs (OIDC plan, REQ-DX-V1, --format json stderr contract, packing vs upload wording, ROAD-TO-V1) with observed current behaviour, docs-only, under trail #374 in worktree wp-docs-reconcile-alpha.
summary.outcome: Edited the docs, ran just doc-check and just pre-push (both exit 0), pushed the branch and opened PR #623 linked to trail #374 at commit 9fa8d911d. Signature was not verified after pushing, and the PR body was not set.

repo: Callisto's generated release workflow allows `id-token: write` only on the `attest` job (no checkout, no run step), not `build-artifact`; the policy check is in .github/tests/verify-release-workflow-policy.sh.

With --format json a failed command leaves stdout empty and ends stderr with one JSON error document, exit 1. Clap argument-parsing errors print usage text and exit 2. Output from tools the command ran (e.g. git `fatal:`) can precede the JSON.
There is no docs/cli directory; the JSON stderr contract is stated only in README.md and docs/stability.md (docs/specs/cli.json already described it).

For npm packages, the workspace's own manager (npm/pnpm/yarn/bun) packs the tarball but `npm publish <tarball>` uploads it, so npm auth and scoped-registry routing apply and Yarn/Bun registry settings are not used. docs/publishing.md already said this.
CLI, config and report surfaces are covered by `callisto schema` output checked in crates/callisto-cli/tests/schema_guard_test.rs and snapshot tests under crates/callisto-cli/tests/snapshots.
Registry binding is proven for Cargo; npm/PyPI evidence comes from the `just verify-real` fixture, which is not part of `just ci`.

code.finding: Schema guard test checks the `callisto schema` output; this is the existing coverage cited in place of cargo-semver-checks.

workflow: Observing the real binary with failing commands (--format json) was needed to record the actual stderr contract rather than trusting existing docs.
Use /usr/bin/git explicitly when the shell git is wrapped or aliased; `entire trail link` and `entire trail ci-pr` handle trail linking and PR creation.

friction: Several initial Bash calls were repeated or reworked, e.g. the git fetch and merge --ff-only calls and the rtk read variant.
The probe loop with `release inspect nofile` and `status --nope` needed a probe script and re-runs to get usable output.
just pre-push first hit a sandbox network block on launch.moonrepo.app and passed only after the host was allowed; one run needed TaskStop and a rerun.
Stray e.txt and o.txt probe output files ended up in the modified-files list.
open_items: PR #623 body is unset; use `gh pr edit 623 --body-file` to add PR-specific text.
The commit signature was not verified after pushing.
Not checked whether the snapshot tests cover config formats, which the ROAD-TO-V1 wording now implies.
Hosted OIDC publishing against real registries remains unverified, as the docs now say.
Fallback of npm and twine to OIDC when tokens are unset is documented but not tested on real packages or projects.
